scopeNote: Seven continuous sections with provisional coverage-driven counts, not official exam weights.

sourceChecks.source: ESC 2025 pericarditis diagnostic and treatment tables
checked: Table 4 separates compatible presentation from additional criteria; definite requires more than one additional criterion, possible requires one.
Tables 13 and 14 checked for anti-inflammatory regimens, prednisone 0.2-0.5 mg/kg/day and slow taper below 15 mg/day.
CRP-positive and CMR-supported CRP-normal resistant inflammatory IL-1 pathways distinguished.
Original Figure 5 checked for possible/definite certainty and duration scheme.
TTE first-line, CMR tissue interpretation and residual LGE limitations checked.
Named ACC activity restriction recommendation distinguished from high-risk myocarditis.

sourceChecks.source: Primary ECG and triage studies plus imaging guidance
checked: Spodick and PR clues do not independently exclude STEMI.
Prospective high-risk indicators include fever, subacute course, large effusion/tamponade and treatment failure.
Imaging modalities answer complementary anatomical, physiological and tissue questions.

sourceChecks.source: ICAP, CORP and CORP-2 randomized colchicine trials
checked: ICAP higher-weight 0.5 mg twice daily and lower-weight 0.5 mg daily for three months; no loading schedule.
ICAP incessant/recurrent outcome 16.7% vs 37.5%, not a mortality endpoint.
CORP first recurrence and CORP-2 multiple-recurrence populations and reported recurrence rates distinguished.
Renal/hepatic impairment plus P-gp or strong CYP3A4 inhibitors is contraindicated in the cited colchicine tablet label.
Aspirin preferred after MI; ACS table gives 500-1000 mg every six to eight hours when needed; dedicated post-MI trial evidence is limited.
Colchicine pregnancy compatibility distinguished from late-pregnancy NSAID restrictions.
FDA twenty-to-thirty-week limitation and avoidance from about thirty weeks distinguished from low-dose aspirin indications.

sourceChecks.source: RHAPSODY, AIRTRIP, IL-1 labels and long-term extension
checked: Both named trials use active run-in and randomized withdrawal; effects cannot be presented as active head-to-head comparisons.
Rilonacept adult dose independently verified as 320 mg ONCE then 160 mg weekly; the daily-looking loading entry in the ESC extracted table must not be followed.
AIRTRIP selected twenty-one patients; anakinra 2 mg/kg/day up to 100 mg/day; withdrawal events 2/11 vs 9/10.
Anakinra label neutrophil and renal precautions reviewed; rilonacept label indication, pediatric weight schedule, infections and lipids reviewed.
Long-term extension suspension group 6/8 recurrence; small nonrandomized treatment-decision observation, not proof of mandatory lifelong therapy.

sourceChecks.source: Effusion surveillance, cause-directed treatment and fluid interpretation
checked: Chronic noninflammatory asymptomatic idiopathic large-effusion observation is a selected phenotype, not a general no-drainage rule.
Hypothyroid replacement doses and CAD caution checked.
ASN intensified-dialysis schedule is explicitly a published clinical approach, not a universal mandatory regimen.
Pericardial-fluid Light classification limitation distinguished from pleural rules.

sourceChecks.source: TB diagnosis, IMPI and national treatment distinction
checked: Negative pericardial Xpert does not exclude TB; ADA and blood IGRA have different diagnostic roles.
IMPI primary-composite neutrality and HIV-related malignancy caution checked against ESC 2025.
ESC six-month standard and India NTEP ethambutol continuation distinction checked; shorter pulmonary regimens not extrapolated.
ESC purulent-drainage and minimum antimicrobial-duration text read.

sourceChecks.source: Tamponade timing, loading context and drainage
checked: RA atrial-relaxation/ventricular-systolic timing distinguished from RV early ventricular diastolic collapse.
Respiratory mitral/tricuspid ranges and spontaneous-versus-positive-pressure interpretation checked.
Low volume and high right-sided pressure alter classic signs; postoperative localized collections can require TEE.
Type A dissection requires source repair; controlled minimal rescue drainage is distinct from routine complete evacuation.
Initial staged drainage guidance is conditional, not a fixed 500-mL stopping rule.

sourceChecks.source: Constrictive physiology and reversibility primary studies
checked: Original Mayo septal-shift plus medial e-prime >=9 or expiratory hepatic reversal ratio >=0.79 checked; named study performance kept population-specific.
Annulus reversus and paradoxus are distinct, and normal pericardial thickness does not exclude physiological constriction.
Simultaneous respiratory ventricular measurements distinguished from nonspecific static pressure equalization.
Effusive-constrictive pressure definition checked against original prospective study and current guideline.
Pilot inflammatory-reversibility association distinguished from guaranteed treatment response; current 3-6-month trial and permanent-constriction surgical framework checked.

sourceChecks.source: Post-cardiac injury criteria and postoperative colchicine trials
checked: At least two of five PCIS findings and inflammatory context checked.
COPPS postoperative initiation distinguished from COPPS-2 preoperative schedule.
COPPS-2 primary PPS reduction, nonsignificant ITT AF/effusion outcomes and increased adverse events checked in primary abstract.
Established postoperative-effusion colchicine trial is negative for volume reduction/late tamponade prevention; not conflated with syndrome prevention.

editorialReviewProgress.remaining: None for the author-review gate; independent clinician review is not claimed.
changes: Question 3 is a direct first-line imaging question without an unnecessary contrast vignette.
Question 4 now compares actual competing imaging tests instead of implausible etiological claims from enhancement.
Question 16 explains the ESC 2025 incessant category for ongoing-treatment/taper flares and separates it from the conventional ACC duration terminology.
Question 18 identifies an on-treatment flare without implying a fully off-treatment recurrence.
Question 28 distinguishes the ESC/WHO-style 2HRZE/4HR description from India NTEP 2HRZE/4HRE.
Question 29 includes the current guideline minimum three-week antimicrobial duration with response-guided individualization.
Numerical teaching emphasis includes relevant microgram, velocity and fluid-volume units.
Q9 is a direct trial-regimen question; Q10 correct option shortened.
Q12 now compares concrete prednisone, pulse methylprednisolone and steroid-sparing strategies without giveaway qualifications.
Q14 removes the explicit high-risk-myocarditis label from the competing duration strategy.
Q15 adds the pregnancy-specific ESC preferred prednisone target up to 20 mg/day when feasible.
Q17 chronology clarified; Q18 compares NSAID addition, steroid increase, azathioprine and anakinra with matching rationales and an explicit NSAID regimen.
Q19 now contains standalone anakinra/rilonacept mechanisms, reference regimens and drug-specific monitoring rather than depending on adjacent questions.
Q22 qualifies off-label interval changes; Q23 now tests the observed extension outcome with plausible competing findings rather than an unsupported dose-escalation plan.
Q24 compares anatomical size categories rather than implausible EF-based size reasoning.
Q25 compares thyroid replacement with or without specific adjuncts; Q26 removes mandatory-drainage giveaway wording.
Q27 and Q28 correct options shortened; Q28 removes universal-steroid wording from the competing strategy.
Q29 duplicated antibiotic sentence removed and drainage alternatives improved; Q30 compares actual renal-pericarditis management plans.
Q31 specifies the access limitation that favors surgery and compares a genuine catheter-based alternative; Q32 uses a medical topic title.
Coverage audit added electrical alternans as a distinct high-yield decision after pulsus paradoxus; final count is 54, not a fixed quota. Later question indices shifted by one.
Final Q35 phase distractor no longer uses the temporally ambiguous after-the-QRS wording.
Final Q40 and Q41 compare realistic imaging or procedural sequences; final Q42 distinguishes immediate repair from a selected rescue drainage bridge.
Final Q45 uses consistently timed hepatic-vein measures across options; Q46 compares classical binary annular relationships without diagnostic giveaway claims.
Final Q47 uses diagnosis names without leading qualifiers; Q48 compares realistic investigations and supplies the systolic-area-index formula.
Final Q50 and Q52 include standalone reference anti-inflammatory regimens; Q51 and Q54 remove leading or self-defeating option qualifications.
TB explanation includes the cause-specific four-to-eight-week deterioration threshold; drainage explanation includes the low-output catheter-removal criterion.
Ratio thresholds 0.34, 0.79 and 1.1 receive the requested numerical emphasis.

limitations: Author source checking is not independent clinician review.
Structural validation is not proof of clinical completeness.
